title: Presence, Power, and Warmth
coreMove: Diagnose whether the room is missing attention, credibility, or goodwill before changing your behavior.
sourcePressure: The source names presence, power, and warmth as the three keys to charisma: presence helps people feel seen, power creates credibility and impact, and warmth signals trust and goodwill.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version lists three nice traits. The useful version shows how one missing signal changes the whole read.

hook: Presence power and warmth are the secret

exampleSpecs.domain: an airline gate safety briefing after a mechanical delay
exampleSpecs.audience: a frontline supervisor who sounds competent but not attentive
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether passengers believe the crew has both facts and concern before boarding resumes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she looks up from the operations tablet, names the delay plainly, then adds the specific passenger concern the crowd has been whispering about
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a gate monitor blinking red beside a coiled microphone cord

exampleSpecs.domain: a neonatal unit handoff between two nurses and frightened parents
exampleSpecs.audience: a warm professional whose credibility can vanish if she seems too soft
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the parents trust the next twelve-hour care plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse keeps one hand near the incubator log, states the oxygen number precisely, and then turns to ask the parents what they noticed overnight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tiny knit cap folded beside an incubator log

exampleSpecs.domain: a city planning hearing about a protected bike corridor
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical expert who must be legible to residents
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the room sees both competence and respect for daily street life
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he decides to leave the crash map projected while he steps away from the lectern and repeats a resident's exact block name before citing the data
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded crash map pinned with colored tabs

exampleSpecs.domain: an indoor climbing wall where a belay instructor wins trust from a nervous adult beginner
exampleSpecs.audience: a skilled operator who forgets that power without warmth feels scary
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the beginner leans back into the rope instead of quitting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the instructor asks her to check the knot with him, names exactly how the belay device works, then waits until she says she is ready before taking slack
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a figure-eight knot resting against a chalk-dusted harness

exampleSpecs.domain: a boutique lender meeting with a couple buying a fishing boat business
exampleSpecs.audience: a financial expert who can sound cold when assessing risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the borrowers accept a hard condition without feeling dismissed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she slides the cash-flow schedule forward, marks the risky month, and says what she wants to protect for them before naming the condition
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tide calendar tucked under a loan amortization sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant pass where an executive chef corrects a plating error mid-service
exampleSpecs.audience: a high-power reader whose urgency can erase warmth
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a new line cook fixes the dish without shutting down
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the barked correction with the reset where the chef points to the sauce ring, lowers his voice, and gives one exact next move
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a white plate with sauce bleeding across the rim

skillTargets: identify which charisma signal is missing in a scenario
choose behavior that restores presence without weakening power
evaluate tradeoffs when credibility and goodwill are both at stake

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next substantive exchange, ask which signal the other person most needs from you: full attention, credible weight, or visible goodwill.
